title: Memory: what the agent can still see
objective: Watch an agent forget when its context fills up, and compare three fixes: a bigger context, compaction into a summary, and notes kept outside the context.

sources.title: Anthropic: Effective context engineering for AI agents (Sep 2025): context is a finite resource; compaction; structured note-taking
Claude Platform docs: Using the Messages API ("The Messages API is stateless, which means that you always send the full conversational history")

simplifies: The model here is a script with fixed rules, not a real AI: a real model's choices vary between runs, and it might give up, ask for help or retry differently. Budgets here are tiny so forgetting shows quickly; real context windows are far bigger, but long agent runs still fill them. Token counts are illustrative.

challenges.title: The forgetful agent
challenges.prompt: The context holds 60 tokens and the agent keeps everything until it falls out. Get the right restaurant using at most 400 tokens.

predict.prompt: The fifth answer arrives, and the first one is pushed out of the context. What will the agent do?

options.text: Ask the first teammate again, without knowing it already did
options.explanation: Right. Once an answer is out of view, the model can't tell it ever asked.
The model only knows what's in its context right now.
It hasn't seen all five answers, so its rule says keep asking.

challenges.hint: The answers fall out of view one by one. What could keep their gist in less space?
challenges.explain: Compaction replaces dropped answers with a short summary of the facts, so the agent stops re-asking. Notes would work too, but each one costs an extra turn: look at the tokens.

challenges.title: A tiny context
challenges.prompt: The context holds only 40 tokens: even a summary of five answers doesn't fit. Get the right restaurant.
challenges.hint: What survives no matter how small the context is?
challenges.explain: Notes live outside the context, so they survive any budget. The price is an extra turn per note.

challenges.title: Memory you don't need
challenges.prompt: The context holds 160 tokens, plenty for every answer, but the agent writes notes anyway. Get the right restaurant using at most 330 tokens.
challenges.hint: Is the extra turn per note buying anything here?
challenges.explain: When everything fits, notes only add turns and tokens. Match the memory approach to the task's size.

quiz.prompt: Why do notes survive when old context is dropped?

options.explanation: The model keeps nothing between calls; the app stores the notes.
Short helps, but they survive because they're stored separately.

options.text: They are kept outside the context and added back on every turn
options.explanation: Right. Anthropic calls this structured note-taking: notes persist outside the context window.

options.text: Speed for accuracy: it makes the model slower but always right
options.explanation: A summary can lose facts; it isn't a guarantee.

options.text: Detail for space: a summary keeps the gist in fewer tokens, and anything cut from it is gone
options.explanation: Right. Too small a budget, and even the summary can't hold what matters.
It loses detail and needs a summary to be written.
